name: Block destructive shell commands
oneLine: Blocks rm -rf, disk tools, force pushes, and destructive git commands before they run.
description: Fires before Bash tool calls. The script scans the command for a deliberately narrow list of destructive patterns (rm -rf, mkfs, dd to devices, fork bombs, git reset --hard, git clean -f, force push) and denies the call with a reason. Narrow on purpose: a broad blocker cries wolf and gets disabled.
recoveryNote: The deny reason names the pattern that matched, so you can run the command yourself in a terminal if it was intentional. Adjust the case list to your taste - it is meant to be edited.
installSteps: Save the script to .claude/hooks/block-destructive-commands.sh and chmod +x it.
Add the config fragment to settings.json.
testSteps: Positive: ask Claude to 'run rm -rf /tmp/junk' - the call must be denied with the reason shown.
Negative: ask Claude to 'run rm -rf node_modules'... also blocked (the pattern is literal). If you want that allowed, whitelist it in the script.
Negative: 'ls -la' and 'git status' pass through normally.
verifiedAgainst: Claude Code hooks reference, event/matcher schema checked 2026-09-10
seoTitle: Block destructive shell commands - Claude Code hook
